title: Bank of Japan MPM decision + Outlook Report (MPM Apr 27-28, 2027 — first meeting after the food consumption-tax cut takes effect)
source: NEWS: boj.or.jp 'Monetary Policy Meetings' schedule page (en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/), re-fetched raw direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 41,959 bytes) and column-parsed out of the HTML by this session. The 'Table : 2027' row parses as ['Apr. 27 (Tues.), 28 (Wed.)', 'Apr. 28 (Wed.)', 'May 12 (Wed.)', 'June 16 (Wed.)'] against the header 'Date of MPM | Outlook Report (The Bank's View) | Summary of Opinions | MPM Minutes' — the dated Outlook column is the primary evidence that this IS an Outlook Report meeting. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the sibling BoJ entries: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has FED: and no slot for any other central bank, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and a schedule published ~20 months ahead is the most movable kind
notes: Proposed during the boj-decision-2027-01-22 initial research (2026-09-05) for one specific reason: it is the FIRST MPM after Japan's food consumption-tax cut takes effect on 2027-04-01 (japan-food-tax-cut-2027-04-01, estimate — 8% to 1% for two years, announced by PM Takaichi, LDP-approved and pending Diet passage as of 2026-08-07 per News On Japan and vatcalc.com), and the first Outlook Report that must project a fiscal year whose CPI carries the cut for its entire span. FY2027 runs 2027-04-01 to 2028-03-31; the cut covers all of it. The BoJ's July-2026 Outlook put the FY2027 core-CPI median at +2.4% (revised up from +2.3% in April) and FY2028 at +2.0%, and the bank's standing projection footnote strips 'the effects of consumption tax HIKES' — wording written for 2014 and 2019, not for a cut. Whether that convention is extended to a cut is decided in January 2027 and first tested against realised data here. SAME CHANNEL, SAME CAVEAT AS THE OTHER BoJ ENTRIES: yen funding and global term premium are both second-order for a US equity book and both already owned by the FOMC ledgers; symbols is empty and no house playbook is rates- or FX-keyed. Second reason this venue matters: it is one of only TWO MPMs inside Q2 2027 (with Jun. 10-11, same primary table), which is the window Reuters' 2026-07-23 poll found '70% of economists anticipate the BoJ to hike rates to at least 1.50%' in — so the consensus level target has two venues and this is the first.
